'''Times Tables Rock Stars'''  (also known as '''TT Rockstars''') is a [[Bedford]]-based educational maths application and website created by Bruno Reddy and [[Maths Circle Ltd]] that focuses on [[GCSE]] level maths.<ref name="Bedford">{{cite web |last= Roffe|first= Erica|date= 25 June 2020|title= 10-year-old becomes record breaking Times Tables Rock Star|url= https://www.bedfordindependent.co.uk/10-year-old-becomes-record-breaking-times-tables-rock-star/|website= |location= |publisher= [[Bedford Independent]]|access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref name="nottingham">{{cite web |last= Sherdley|first= Rebecca|date= 26 Jun 2020|title= Incredible video shows ten-year-old answer 196 maths questions in a minute on Times Tables Rock Stars|url= https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/nottingham-news/watch-speedy-ten-year-old-4265872|website= |location= |publisher= [[Nottingham Post]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref name="cochlear">{{cite web |last= Ames|first= Helen|date= 11 October 2022|title= Local children inspire the makers of Times Tables Rock Stars|url= https://www.newcastle.gov.uk/citylife-news/education/local-children-inspire-makers-times-tables-rock-stars|website= newcastle.gov.uk|location= |publisher= [[Newcastle City Council]]|url-status= |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20221011141929/https://www.newcastle.gov.uk/citylife-news/education/local-children-inspire-makers-times-tables-rock-stars|archive-date= 11 Oct 2022|access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref>

==History==

Times Tables Rock Stars was created in 2010 by Bruno Reddy, a [[Education in the United Kingdom#Stages|secondary school]] maths teacher.
Reddy wore a wig, and played [[rock music]] while holding a blow-up guitar at the beginning of his lessons, in which he encouraged his pupils to answer quick-fire maths questions.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title= About Us|url=https://ttrockstars.com/about-us/|website= |location= |publisher= Times Tables Rock Stars |access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> Reddy launched the application to help his pupils increase their speed with answering questions about [[Multiplication table|times tables]].<ref>{{cite web |last= George|first= Martin|date= 21 Jan 2019|title= Edtech success: Bruno Reddy of Times Tables Rock Stars|url=https://www.tes.com/magazine/archive/edtech-success-bruno-reddy-times-tables-rock-stars |website= |location= |publisher= [[TES (magazine)|TES]]|access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref>

==Gameplay==
[[File:Times_Tables_Rock_Stars_gameplay.png|thumb|left|The gameplay of Times Tables Rock Stars consists of players going up the ranks as a rockstar by answering multiplication and division questions]]
Gameplay consists of answering as many [[multiplication]] and [[Division (mathematics)|division]] questions as possible in a specific amount of time.<ref name="Belfast">{{cite web |last= Bain|first= Mark|date= 27 October 2025|title= Belfast student top of the class in maths after beating more than 17,000 kids across the island|url= https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/education/belfast-student-top-of-the-class-in-maths-after-beating-more-than-17000-kids-across-the-island/a852403882.html|website= |location= |publisher= [[Belfast Telegraph]]|url-status= |archive-url= https://archive.today/20251027081826/https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/education/belfast-student-top-of-the-class-in-maths-after-beating-more-than-17000-kids-across-the-island/a852403882.html|archive-date= 27 Oct 2025|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref name="thanet">{{cite web |last= Bailes|first= Kathy|date= 30 June 2020|title= Upton pupil Cobey is a global Times Tables Rock Star|url= https://theisleofthanetnews.com/2020/06/30/upton-pupil-cobey-is-a-global-times-tables-rock-star/|website= |location= |publisher= The Isle of Thanet News|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref>
Players also make their own rock star names and avatars for use in-game. Players earn points for the number of questions they answer, which they can then spend on new clothing items and accessories for their avatar.<ref name="cochlear" /><ref name="avatar">{{cite web |last= Keating|first= Kate|date= 2 Feb 2024|title= Maths lessons rock at Havelock Schools|url= https://www.northantstelegraph.co.uk/education/maths-lessons-rock-at-havelock-schools-4502969|website= |location= |publisher= [[Northamptonshire Evening Telegraph]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref>

[[Ranking|Leaderboards]] are based on every school in a specific area.
Two classes in the same school can compete against each other in "Battle of the Bands" competitions where each class tries to answer more questions in total than the other class.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= 6 March 2018|title= Wybunbury Delves pupils excel in Times Tables Rock Stars contest|url= https://thenantwichnews.co.uk/2018/03/06/wybunbury-delves-pupils-excel-in-times-tables-rock-stars-contest/|website= |location= |publisher= Nantwich News|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref>
The application also hosts several nationwide maths competitions where every school in a certain location competes against each other; Oz Rocks for [[Australia]],<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= 22 April 2021|title= St David's students 'rock' their times tables|url= https://www.cesa.catholic.edu.au/news/69441/st-david-s-students-rock-their-times-tables|website= |location= |publisher= Catholic Education South Australia|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> Ireland Rocks for [[the island of Ireland]] as part of the 20th annual [[Maths Week Ireland]],<ref name="Belfast" /> South Island Rocks for the [[South Island]] of [[New Zealand]], North Island Rocks for the [[North Island]] of New Zealand,<ref>{{cite web |last= Williams|first= Elsie|date= 7 August 2025|title= 'Back in fashion': Times tables make a comeback with modern competition for kids|url= https://www.thepress.co.nz/nz-news/360783883/back-fashion-times-tables-make-comeback-modern-competition-kids|website= |location= |publisher= [[The Press]]|access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last= Burns|first= Adam|date= 7 August 2025|title= 15,000 students compete in Times Tables Rock Stars Mathematics competition
|url= https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/569337/15-000-students-compete-in-times-tables-rock-stars-mathematics-competition|website= |location= |publisher= [[RNZ]]|access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref> Scotland Rocks for [[Scotland]],<ref>{{cite web |last= McMorran|first= Caroline|date= 29 September 2022|title= North-west Sutherland pupils are maths rock stars! Schools shine in national competition|url= https://www.northern-times.co.uk/news/north-west-sutherland-pupils-are-maths-rock-stars-schools-s-289060/|website= |location= |publisher= The Northern Times|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> England Rocks for [[England]],<ref>{{cite web |last= Hubbert|first= Andy|date= 28 Nov 2023|title= Sleaford boy in Top 50 in the country for Times Table Rockstar maths challenge|url= https://www.lincolnshireworld.com/education/sleaford-boy-in-top-50-in-the-country-for-times-table-rockstar-maths-challenge-4426485|website= |location= |publisher= lincolnshireworld.com |access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref> London Rocks for [[London]],<ref>{{cite web |last= Mitchell|first= Chris|date= 4 July 2022|title= Pinner Wood School in Harrow WINS national times table competition|url= https://harrowonline.org/2022/07/04/pinner-wood-school-competition/#google_vignette|website= |location= |publisher= Harrow Online|access-date= 20 Jan 2026}}</ref> Cardiff Rocks for [[Cardiff]], Wales Rocks for [[Wales]], NSPCC Rocks for all of the [[UK]] as part of [[NSPCC Numbers Day]], UAE rocks for the [[United Arab Emirates]], Qatar Rocks for [[Qatar]],<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title= Events|url= https://ttrockstars.com/events/events-online/|website= |location= |publisher= Times Tables Rock Stars|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> Melbourne Rocks for [[Melbourne]]<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title= Melbourne Rocks|url= https://ttrockstars.com/events/events-online-3/melbournerocks2025/|website= |location= |publisher= Times Tables Rock Stars |access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> and Rest of the World Rocks for the Rest of the World.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= 18 March 2024|title= The 'Rest of the World Rocks' Maths Competition - Outstanding Success!|url= https://www.rushallns.ie/News/The-Rest-of-the-World-Rocks-Maths-Competition--Outstanding-Success!/31785/Index.html|website= |location= |publisher= Rushall National School|access-date=}}</ref><ref name="laois1">{{cite web |last= Hartnett|first= Alan|date= 29 March 2023|title= Clever Laois primary school students claim second place in international maths competition|url=https://www.laoistoday.ie/2023/03/29/clever-laois-primary-school-students-claim-second-place-in-international-maths-competition/ |website= |location= |publisher= Laois Today|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last= Ganly|first= Conor|date= 30 March 2023|title= Laois school's out of the world performance in international contest|url= https://www.leinsterexpress.ie/news/schools/1074600/laois-school-s-out-of-the-world-performance-in-international-contest.html|website= |location= |publisher= [[Leinster Express]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref>

==Reception==
Several schools dressed up in costumes inspired by Times Tables Rock Stars after their school gained access to the application.<ref>{{cite web |last= Carter|first= William|date= 11 November 2022|title= Ringstead Church of England Primary School launches Times Tables Rock Stars with funky fancy dress|url= https://www.northantstelegraph.co.uk/news/people/ringstead-church-of-england-primary-school-launches-times-tables-rock-stars-with-funky-fancy-dress-3914727|website= |location= |publisher= [[Northamptonshire Evening Telegraph]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref name="world">{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated-->|date= 28 Feb 2020|title= Louth pupils 'rock' at their times tables!|url= https://www.lincolnshireworld.com/news/uk-news/louth-pupils-rock-at-their-times-tables-2006745|website= |location= |publisher= [[Lincolnshire World]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last= Clarke|first= Lewis|date= 19 November 2025|title= Pupils go full rock star to launch new maths game at Tiverton school|url= https://www.devonlive.com/news/devon-news/gallery/pupils-go-full-rock-star-10655274|website= |location= |publisher= [[Devon Live]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> One primary school in [[Hambridge]] declared February 20 as Times Tables Rock Stars and Numbots day.<ref>{{cite web |last= Manuschka|first= Jacob|date= 27 February 2024|title= Hambridge primary school dresses up for maths activities day|url= https://www.somersetcountygazette.co.uk/news/24145321.hambridge-primary-school-dresses-maths-activities-day/|website= |location= |publisher= [[Somerset County Gazette]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> Several schools described the application as world renowned.<ref name="laois1" /> An article in ''[[The Guardian]]'' stated that the idea seemed counterintuitive, easy to mock and a rather gimmicky approach but also called the idea a success due to the creator's past experience as a former head of maths while being wary of "the way in which various approaches to education can be taken up on a large scale despite schools not necessarily knowing whether they’re actually helping students."<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= 27 Jan 2018|title= Secret Teacher: education should be driven by evidence, not political whims|url= https://www.theguardian.com/teacher-network/2018/jan/27/secret-teacher-education-secretaries-enough-whims-gimmick|website= |location= |publisher= [[The Guardian]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> ''[[The Times]]'' stated that "The [[Tories]] are proposing that children be allowed to opt out of screen-based learning amid fears devices are being used too much in schools" citing Times Tables Rock Stars, [[Duolingo]], [[Spelling Shed]], [[Kahoot]], Seneca and [[Quizlet]] as examples of popular educational technology programs that parents weren't able to opt out of.<ref>{{cite web |last= Eccles|first= Louise|date= 7 September 2025|title= Bring back pen and paper! Calls to scrap 'screen-based homework'|url= https://www.thetimes.com/uk/education/article/screen-based-homework-sophie-winkleman-7knx8hbwl|website= |location= |publisher= [[The Times]]|url-status= |archive-url= https://archive.today/20250911030022/https://www.thetimes.com/uk/education/article/screen-based-homework-sophie-winkleman-7knx8hbwl#selection-1541.0-1541.39|archive-date= 11 Sep 2025|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref>

When Broadwood Primary School in [[Denton Burn]] gained access to the application, the pupils at the school were confused as to why they weren't able to equip [[cochlear implants]] on their avatars when there were already [[hearing aids]] in-game. When contacted about the issue, the developers added cochlear implants to the game.<ref name="cochlear" />

==Guinness World Records==
In 2020 during the [[COVID-19 lockdowns|COVID-19 lockdown]] Times Tables Rock Stars and [[Guinness World Records]] announced a new title; Highest Score achieved on Times Tables Rock Stars in one minute.
Out of the initial 700 official attempts accompanied with video evidence, 10-year-old Nadub Gill from [[Long Eaton]] was the fastest at 196 multiplication questions answered in one minute.<ref name="Bedford" /><ref name="nottingham" /><ref>{{cite web |last= Suggitt|first= Connie|date= 6 July 2020|title= This 10-year-old can answer 196 maths questions correctly in one minute|url= https://kids.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2020/7/this-10-year-old-can-answer-196-maths-questions-correctly-in-one-minute-623211|website= |location= |publisher= [[Guinness World Records]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref> He held the record until he was beaten by Brooke Cressey from [[Sittingbourne]] on 3 December 2021 when she correctly answered 210 questions in one minute.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= 28 Jan 2022|title= The eight-year-old maths genius who can do three sums in a second|url= https://www.itv.com/news/meridian/2022-01-28/the-eight-year-old-maths-genius-who-can-do-three-sums-in-a-second|website= |location= |publisher= [[ITV Studios|ITV]]|access-date=20 Jan 2026}}</ref>
